summary: In ansible-core 2.21, utils.encrypt uses libcrypt/libxcrypt instead of the deprecated passlib, producing compatible but not byte-identical password hashes.
questions: Why do password hashes generated by ansible-core 2.21 differ from before?
Does Ansible still use passlib for password hashing?
Will my existing password hashes still work after upgrading to ansible-core 2.21?

answer_card.title: encrypt uses libcrypt instead of passlib
answer_card.answer_md: In ansible-core 2.21, the `utils.encrypt` functions use **libcrypt/libxcrypt** instead of the deprecated **passlib**. The hashes are compatible, but not exactly the same as before, because passlib did extra processing and formatting. Code using these functions should keep working, but its output won't match earlier Ansible versions.
